What begins to develop in the early weeks?
In the early stage, the brain, spinal cord and other organs and structures begin to form.
Development continues throughout pregnancy and can vary. This general description cannot assess how your baby is doing.
What changes occur in the middle stage?
Bones begin to harden and hearing continues to develop. Movements become stronger as this stage progresses.
These are general changes, not a checklist your baby must meet in a specific week.
What keeps developing in the final stage?
The baby continues to accumulate fat and develop for life outside the womb. They can stretch and move their limbs.
These features describe a broad stage and do not replace assessment by your prenatal care team.
How many prenatal contacts are recommended?
WHO recommends at least eight contacts with health professionals during pregnancy, with the first within the first 12 weeks.
Your care team adapts follow-up to your needs and local guidance. If you haven't started your check-ups yet, arrange prenatal care.
What is an ultrasound before 24 weeks used for?
WHO recommends an ultrasound before 24 weeks to estimate gestational age and help detect multiple pregnancies and fetal anomalies.
Your professional decides when to perform it and explains the results; the app does not interpret examinations.
When are movements usually first felt?
They are usually felt between weeks 16 and 24; in a first pregnancy, they may not be noticed until after week 20.
If you have never felt them by week 24, contact your prenatal care team for assessment.
What should I do if the pattern of movements changes?
If you were already feeling movements and now feel fewer, no longer feel them, or notice a change in their usual pattern, contact your prenatal care team or maternity emergency service immediately.
Do not wait until the next day. A home Doppler cannot confirm that your baby is well.
